question.text: For a non-corporate assessee (e.g. LLP) invested in a Cat III AIF, Alternate Minimum Tax (AMT) per the ITA is levied at what rate (on adjusted total income), excluding surcharge/cess?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook: 'In case of non-corporate assessee, AMT is taxable at the rate of 18.5% (15% in case of co-operative society) (plus applicable surcharge and health and education cess) ... except in cases where option referred to in Section 115BAC/BAD/BAE are exercised.' The Trap: 15% is the MAT rate for corporates (and AMT for co-op societies). 22% is the concessional corporate rate. 30% is the base income-tax rate. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D drills MAT/AMT for Cat I/II LP structures too. XIX-E drills AMT on LLP/trust LPs in Cat III. XXI-B covers AMT for HNI/LLP PMS clients. Both rates (MAT 15% corporate, AMT 18.5% non-corporate) are high-yield trap pairs. Manager's Pro-Tip: LLP LPs in Aravalli or Chambal should be reminded that even if the fund has already MMR-taxed business income, AMT at 18.5% could bite them at the entity level if they have claimed Chapter VI-A or Section 10AA deductions. AMT credit (15 years) partially cushions but creates timing drag.
